cards.title: Hugging Face Holo4: Generalist Computer-Use Agents in 27B Dense and 35B-A3B MoE
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI/ML engineer, Holo4 represents a significant open-weight agentic model release that unifies GUI, code, MCP, and API interaction in a single model — a genuine architectural and training advance worth tracking for agent system design.
cards.summary: Hugging Face releases Holo4 in two sizes (27B dense, 35B-A3B MoE), both available via H Models API. Models interact via GUIs, code, MCP, and APIs interchangeably, trained with supervised and RL on tasks from their Agentic Task Factory. On OSWorld 2.0, Holo4-27B scores 61.7% vs. 81.8% for Opus 5.5. Trajectories and weights (FP16, FP8, GGUF) are fully open-sourced.

cards.title: Telescopic Language Models: A Single Training Run Yields Valid LMs at Every Layer Depth
cards.why_it_matters: For a researcher working on efficient inference or model compression, TLM's stochastic prefix supervision approach directly addresses the failure mode of fixed-exit Matryoshka-style models and cuts quality-budget curve area by 43–44% — a concrete, reproducible training objective result.
cards.summary: Telescopic Language Models (TLMs) use stochastic prefix supervision — randomly truncated capacity-axis prefixes trained against full next-token targets plus one full-capacity pass — producing a valid LM at every layer depth with only two forward-backward passes per step and no architectural changes. On a 200M proxy suite (20B FineWeb-Edu tokens), TLM reduces area under the quality-budget curve by 43–44% vs. fixed-exit Matryoshka suites, matches them at full capacity, and costs ~12% less GPU per run.

cards.title: PDMD: One-Line Fix to Distribution Matching Distillation Stabilizes Video Diffusion at 4 NFE
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on diffusion model distillation or video generation, PDMD's theoretical grounding of why DMD degrades — critic error accumulation — and its near-zero-overhead fix are directly actionable insights for production-quality fast samplers.
cards.summary: PDMD projects out the DMD update component parallel to the student-critic endpoint residual, provably removing a constant fraction of critic error while discarding only a vanishing fraction of ideal DMD signal. Requires a single code-line change with no extra networks or training stages. With Wan2.1 at 4 NFE, PDMD achieves VBench total score 83.73, surpassing matched DMD by 1.03 points; on MiniMax-H3 joint video-audio generation, scores 83.17 visual total, 0.41 above the strongest distilled baseline.

cards.title: UMM-Reflection: Interleaved RL Trains Unified Models to Reflectively Self-Repair Image Generation
cards.why_it_matters: The interleaved RL formulation — sharing one initial image across sibling trajectories so group-relative advantage compares full reflection strategies, with credit flowing across rounds and to both model roles — is a technically novel approach to self-correction in unified multimodal models relevant to agents and RL post-training research.
cards.summary: UMM-Reflection applies RL to complete reflection trajectories within a single unified model that both perceives and generates images. Sibling trajectories share an initial image for group-relative advantage estimation; one trajectory-level advantage updates both reflection tokens and flow-based image revisions jointly. On BAGEL, GenEval improves 12.05 points over SFT; gains also transfer to WISE (+10.97), OneIG-Bench (+3.48), and T2I-CompBench++ (+4.63), all held-out benchmarks.

cards.title: FurE: 10× Faster Animal Fur Reconstruction via PCA Decoder Transferred from Human Hair Data
cards.why_it_matters: The cross-domain transfer trick — using a PCA-based decoder trained on human hair to handle animal fur without animal-fur datasets — is a methodologically interesting trick for any researcher working on neural implicit representations or data-scarce 3D reconstruction.
cards.summary: FurE reconstructs editable, per-strand animal fur from multi-view images without animal-fur training data. It optimizes a root-conditioned latent field decoded via a PCA-based decoder pre-trained on human hair strands, and reconstructs a defurred body using surface-constrained Gaussian Frosting with part-based priors. Achieves 10× speedup in strand training over dense per-strand SOTA while retaining fidelity.
